contentBlocks.body: Clients need errors they can parse. Instead of inventing a new error shape per endpoint, use **Problem Details** (RFC 9457, formerly 7807) with `Content-Type: application/problem+json`. The standard members are `type` (a URI naming the error kind), `title` (a short, fixed summary), `status`, `detail` (this occurrence), and `instance` (the request path). You may add members such as `errors` or `traceId`.

contentBlocks.code:
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://example.com/problems/not-found",
  "title": "Resource not found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "Product 42 was not found.",
  "instance": "/products/42"
}

contentBlocks.body: Clients should branch on `type` (or `status`), never on the English text in `title` or `detail`, which you may reword at any time.

A 500 response must not include the exception message or stack trace: they leak table names, file paths, and sometimes connection strings. Log the details server-side with a correlation id and send the client only a generic title plus that id.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which Content-Type identifies an RFC 9457 error body?

payload.explanation: Problem Details uses the application/problem+json media type (and application/problem+xml for XML).

knowledgeItems.prompt: What should a client use to decide how to handle a problem details error?

choices: The type URI and status code
payload.answer: The type URI and status code
payload.explanation: type and status are stable identifiers. title and detail are human-readable text that may change or be localized.

payload.text: In problem details, the ____ member holds the path of the request that failed.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Convert application errors (not-found, validation, conflict, unexpected) into problem details bodies with the right type, title, status, and detail, without leaking internal error messages.
